newsitem.title: GREECE: Short-end of Greek yield curve up, ecu/drs ranges.
newsitem.headline: Short-end of Greek yield curve up, ecu/drs ranges.

text.p: Short-term depos are firmer 10 to 30 basis points before mid-session, forex forwards from tomnext to two-week were also higher, bonds were drifting slowly to lower levels and ecu/drachma was consolidating below 311, traders said.

"Short depos are firmer 10 to 30 basis points on the liquidity squeeze," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Forwards are steady but for a rise in tomnext til two-week tenors but bid-ask spreads have narrowed."
Dealers said they expected the central bank not to hold its depo tender today to boost the system's liquidity. A pact of 200 billion drachmas for 14-day funds is expiring on Wednesday.
The central bank offered to drain 14-day funds at 11.90 percent in its regular Wednesday tender.
Fixed coupon bonds were stable to lower in early trade following Tuesday's slide that pushed yields a tenth of a point higher on the higher short-term cost of funding, dealers said.
The mark was quoted at 159.06/11 from Tuesday's 159.400 fix, the dollar at 275.57/67 drachmas from 275.160 and the ecu at 310.51/61 from 310.990 drachmas.
The drachma was rangebound against the ecu in early dealings trading around 310.55/60, dealers said.
"Ecu/drachma opened at 310.70/80 and has eased a bit to 310.55/60," a forex dealer at a foreign bank said. "Players sell marks this morning driving ecu/mark up and mark/drachma lower."
The dealer said the upside risk in ecu/drachma was limited with the central bank willing to intervene at 311 or higher.
Bank of Greece sold $30 million, 60 million ecus and 45 million marks for drachmas at the fixing on Tuesday.
